tasks.title: Absolute value without built-in
tasks.prompt: Write a Python function `abs_val(x: int) -> int` that returns the absolute value of the integer x. Do not use the built-in abs function. Handle only integer inputs; you may assume x is int.

tasks.title: Even check
tasks.prompt: Write a Python function `is_even(n: int) -> bool` that returns True if n is even, False otherwise. Assume n is integer.
tasks.reference:
def is_even(n: int) -> bool:
    return n % 2 == 0

tasks.title: Factorial
tasks.prompt: Write a Python function `factorial(n: int) -> int` that returns the factorial of n (n!). Assume n >= 0. Raise ValueError if n < 0.

tasks.title: Fibonacci number
tasks.prompt: Write a Python function `fib(n: int) -> int` that returns the nth Fibonacci number where fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1. Assume n >= 0.

tasks.title: Merge two sorted lists
tasks.prompt: Write a Python function `merge_sorted(a: list[int], b: list[int]) -> list[int]` that merges two sorted lists of integers into a new sorted list. Do not modify inputs. Assume a and b are sorted in ascending order.

tasks.title: Binary search first occurrence
tasks.prompt: Write a Python function `binary_search(arr: list[int], target: int) -> int` that returns the index of the first occurrence of target in sorted list arr, or -1 if not present. Assume arr is sorted in ascending order.

tasks.title: Merge intervals with touching endpoints
tasks.prompt:
Write a Python function `merge_intervals(intervals)` that merges a list of closed integer intervals. Rules:
1. Each interval is a two-element list `[start, end]` with `start <= end`; the input list may be in any order.
2. Intervals that overlap OR merely touch (`next.start <= current.end`) must be merged into one interval.
3. Return a list of two-element lists `[start, end]`, sorted by start ascending, with no two intervals overlapping or touching.
4. Empty input returns `[]`.
5. Do not mutate the input list or its inner lists.
6. Zero-length intervals (start == end) are valid and merge with any interval that contains or touches that point.

tasks.title: Roman numerals with canonical validation
tasks.prompt:
Write a Python function `roman_to_int(s)` that converts a canonical Roman numeral to an integer in 1..3999. Rules:
1. `s` is a non-empty `str` containing only the uppercase symbols `I V X L C D M`; empty strings, non-strings, lowercase, or any other character must raise `ValueError`.
2. Only these subtractive pairs are legal and each counts as one unit: `IV`=4, `IX`=9, `XL`=40, `XC`=90, `CD`=400, `CM`=900. Any other subtractive form is invalid.
3. `I`, `X`, `C` and `M` may repeat at most three times consecutively; `V`, `L` and `D` may never repeat.
4. The numeral must be canonical: re-encoding the resulting value must reproduce `s` exactly (so `IIII`, `VV`, `IC`, `IM` and `MMMM` are invalid).
5. Any invalid input must raise `ValueError`; the function must never return a number for a non-canonical numeral.

tasks.title: Semver-style compare with pre-release tags
tasks.prompt:
Write a Python function `compare_versions(a, b)` returning -1, 0 or 1. Rules:
1. A version is `core` or `core-pre`. `core` is one or more dot-separated identifiers that each consist only of ASCII digits (leading zeros allowed, compared numerically). `pre` is one or more dot-separated identifiers that each consist only of ASCII letters, digits or `-`.
2. Compare the numeric cores left to right; a missing core identifier counts as 0, so `1.0` and `1.0.0` are equal.
3. A version WITHOUT a pre-release outranks the same core WITH one.
4. Compare pre-release identifiers left to right. Two numeric identifiers compare by integer value; two non-numeric identifiers compare by ASCII order (case-sensitive); a numeric identifier ranks lower than a non-numeric one.
5. If all shared identifiers are equal, fewer pre-release identifiers rank lower (`1.0.0-alpha` < `1.0.0-alpha.1`).
6. Raise `ValueError` for: a non-string or empty input, an empty core identifier (`1..2`), a non-digit core identifier, an empty pre-release (`1-`), an empty pre-release identifier (`1-a..b`), or a pre-release character outside letters/digits/`-` (for example `+`).

tasks.title: Cron field expansion with validation
tasks.prompt:
Write a Python function `expand_cron_field(field, lo, hi)` that expands one cron field into a sorted list of unique integers in `lo..hi` inclusive. Rules:
1. `field` is a comma-separated list of items; whitespace around the field and around each item is ignored. An empty field or empty item raises `ValueError`.
2. Legal item forms are exactly: `*`, `*/S`, `N`, `A-B`, and `A-B/S`, where `N`, `A`, `B`, `S` are base-10 integer strings. `N/S` is illegal and must raise `ValueError`.
3. `*` means every value from `lo` to `hi`; `*/S` means `lo, lo+S, ...` up to `hi`; `A-B` means `A..B` inclusive; `A-B/S` means `A, A+S, ...` up to and including `B`.
4. Every number must satisfy `lo <= value <= hi`, `S >= 1`, and `A <= B`; otherwise raise `ValueError`. Values that are not integers (`a`, `1.5`, `-1`) raise `ValueError`.
5. The result is ascending with duplicates removed and must not depend on item order in the field; an item may overlap another.
